questions.question: Find the odd one out: 2, 4, 6, 9, 10
questions.explanation: All numbers except 9 are even. 9 is odd.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 16, 25, 36, 40, 49
questions.explanation: 16, 25, 36 and 49 are perfect squares. 40 is not.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 11, 13, 17, 21, 23
questions.explanation: 11, 13, 17 and 23 are prime. 21 = 3 × 7 is composite.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³, 64 = 4³ and 125 = 5³ are cubes. 100 is not a perfect cube.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: A, E, I, O, K
questions.explanation: A, E, I and O are vowels. K is a consonant.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 12, 18, 24, 30, 35
questions.explanation: 12, 18, 24 and 30 are multiples of 6. 35 is not.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: ABC, DEF, GHI, JKM
questions.explanation: The groups are consecutive letters in order. JKL would fit, but JKM skips L.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: BDF, HJL, NPR, TVW
questions.explanation: Inside each group the letters are two places apart. TVW has gaps 2 and 1, so it breaks the pattern.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 200
questions.explanation: 121 = 11², 144 = 12² and 169 = 13² are squares. 200 is not.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 6-8-11
questions.explanation: The first three satisfy a² + b² = c² (9 + 16 = 25, 25 + 144 = 169, 64 + 225 = 289). For 6-8-11, 36 + 64 = 100, which is not 121.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9
questions.explanation: 2, 3, 5 and 7 are prime. 9 = 3 × 3 is not.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: AZ, BY, CX, DV
questions.explanation: The pairs are letters and their opposites (positions add to 27). D pairs with W, so DV is wrong.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 14, 21, 28, 36, 42
questions.explanation: 14, 21, 28 and 42 are multiples of 7. 36 is not.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: CF, FI, IL, LO, OS
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by 3 and the next group starts where the previous ended: CF, FI, IL, LO, OR. OS breaks the pattern.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 1, 4, 9, 16, 24, 36
questions.explanation: 1, 4, 9, 16 and 36 are squares of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. 24 is not a perfect square.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 17, 19, 23, 27, 29
questions.explanation: 17, 19, 23 and 29 are primes. 27 = 3³ is not.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: AC, EG, IK, MO, PR
questions.explanation: Each pair is two letters apart, and each pair starts four letters after the previous one: A, E, I, M, Q. So QS would fit, not PR.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: ACE, GIK, MOQ, SUX
questions.explanation: Each group has a gap of 2 between its letters and the first letters move by 6 (A, G, M, S). SUW would fit; SUX has gaps 2 and 3.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 78
questions.explanation: All numbers except 78 are multiples of 11. 78 = 6 × 13.
